approved: Social Security Legislation Amendment (Streamlined Participation Requirements and Other Measures) Bill 2022

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2022-03-30.210.1) to the usual [second reading](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) motion, which is "*that the bill be read for a second time*" - parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill. Because this vote failed, the usual second reading motion will remain unchanged. ### Amendment text > *At the end of the motion, add ", but the Senate:* > > *(a) notes that punitive mutual obligations have unfairly restricted people's access to income support; and* > > *(b) calls on the Government to abolish the Work for the Dole program and provide income support to everyone who needs it".*

The speaker moved a second reading amendment expressing grave concerns about rushing the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Streamlined Participation Requirements and Other Measures) Bill 2021, noting 1.5 million Australians looking for more work and impacts on employment service providers. The speaker confirmed Labor would support the bill once government amendments removed schedule 8, which saved $192 million by delaying first payments to recipients, and ensured ethical use of technology with enforceable codes of conduct.

The speaker opposed the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Streamlined Participation Requirements and Other Measures) Bill 2021, arguing that schedule 8 would delay payments for new jobseekers using online services by up to 10 days, costing an estimated 144,000 people between $300 and $450 per year, while the government had closed Centrelink shopfronts such as the Braddon office in Canberra. Labor moved amendments to remove schedule 8 and add protections for principal carer parents and jobseekers with partial capacity to work, along with a digital code of ethics.

The speaker opposed schedule 8 of the Social Security Legislation Amendment (Streamlined Participation Requirements and Other Measures) Bill 2021, arguing it would delay payments for 144,000 new jobseekers by up to 10 days, costing them $300–$450, and supported the bill only if that schedule is removed.
